what: Wabtec makes the equipment that runs freight and passenger railways: locomotives, braking systems, signalling, and the aftermarket parts and services that keep them running. George Westinghouse invented the air brake that started the company in 1869.
customers: Freight railways in North America and worldwide, passenger transit authorities, and mining companies.
money: locomotives, components, digital systems and aftermarket services
braking, doors and systems for passenger trains and metros
moat: Safety-critical equipment that is certified into railway operations and then serviced for decades, with an installed base that generates recurring parts revenue.
risks: Freight rail volumes have been soft, which delays locomotive orders
Debt of about $7 billion against under $500 million of cash
Transit projects depend on government budgets
Return on invested capital of about 8% is modest
opportunities: Revenue grew about 8% last year with a backlog stretching years out
Aftermarket parts and services are about half of freight revenue and far steadier than new builds
Railway operators are modernising ageing locomotive fleets
watch: The order backlog and freight segment margin.
